title: Testing for Weak Password Change or Reset Functionalities
description: Nested categorical questionnaire for ATHN-09 password reset assessment. Categories a-g map to the primary reset mechanisms and their sub-controls. Some categories ARE the question; others have multiple sub-questions.

questions.question: Is the password reset endpoint protected against rate limiting?
Is the password reset flow vulnerable to SQL Injection?
Does the password reset flow lack MFA?
Does the login flow lack MFA?
Does the user get sent a new password by email?
questions.note: If Yes, this is likely compromised — review sub-questions

questions.question: Is the user forced to change the password on initial login?
Is the password securely generated (sufficient entropy)?
Is the user's EXISTING password sent to them (plaintext storage indicator)?
Are the reset emails sent from a domain with anti-spoofing protection (SPF, DKIM, DMARC)?
Is email considered a sufficiently secure channel for credential delivery?

questions_categories.name: Password Reset Link Sent by Email

questions.question: Does the user get an email with a password reset link?
Does the reset link use HTTPS?
Can the reset link be used multiple times?
Does the reset link expire if it remains unused?
Is the reset token sufficiently long and random (high entropy)?
Does the reset link contain a User ID (leaks account enumeration)?
Does a Google dork expose the reset link (indexed by search engines)?
Are reset emails sent from a domain with anti-spoofing protection (SPF, DKIM, DMARC)?
Does the user get a reset token / link over SMS?
Is the SMS token sufficiently long and random?
Can the SMS token be used multiple times?
Does the SMS token expire if it remains unused?
Are rate limits in place for the SMS token endpoint?
Is SMS considered a sufficiently secure channel for authentication?
questions.note: SMS is vulnerable to SIM-swapping and SS7 attacks. NIST 800-63B designates it RESTRICTED.
